clue.text: You presumably cross off what you're doing, right?

indicators.note: taking something off means removing it, so the word before is struck out of the phrase that follows

parts.note: what the solver is doing right now is a crossword puzzle
the word to be struck out, taken literally
R is the standard abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A teasing question to the solver: surely you tick off clues as you go, don't you?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross off' reads as ticking off solved clues, but it is an instruction: remove CROSS from CROSSWORD PUZZLE, then add R.
explanation.definitionFit: The person solving this clue is by definition someone who tackles verbal brainteasers, a word-puzzler.

clue.text: Best public act

parts.note: out as in out in the open, known to all
to do is to act

explanation.surface: The finest performance put on for an audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Best' looks like an adjective but is a verb, meaning to beat.
explanation.definitionFit: To best someone is to beat or surpass them, which is what outdo means.

clue.text: Exhausted girl in town and county

parts.note: done in the sense of worn out
an informal word for a girl

explanation.surface: A tired young woman somewhere out in the provinces.
explanation.definitionFit: Donegal is both a county in the north-west of Ireland and a town within it.

clue.text: Did drugs when cycling? Here's the outcome

indicators.note: cycling means rotating, so the end of the phrase moves round to the front

parts.note: to shoot up is to inject drugs

explanation.surface: A doping scandal in professional cycling and its consequences.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cycling' suggests the sport, which drugs help the surface along; it really means moving UP from the end to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: An upshot is the final result or consequence of something.

clue.text: South African issue over GMT

parts.note: the Zulu are a people of South Africa

indicators.note: turned over means flipped, so the word for issue is read backwards

parts.note: to emit is to give out, issue

explanation.surface: A complaint from South Africa about Greenwich Mean Time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' looks like a noun but is the verb, giving EMIT, which is turned around.
explanation.definitionFit: Zulu time is the military and aviation name for Coordinated Universal Time, the successor to Greenwich Mean Time.

clue.text: Obsolete opening deleted from message in court

indicators.note: removing the opening means dropping the first letter of the word

parts.note: a text message
taken as written
Ct is the abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: A legal note that an outdated introduction was struck from a statement read in court.
explanation.definitionFit: Extinct means no longer in existence or use, which is what obsolete describes.

clue.text: Fake blogs weakened foundation for AI?

indicators.note: something fake is made up or concocted, so the letters that follow are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of these two words

explanation.surface: Bogus online posts have undermined the data that artificial intelligence is built on.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that a knowledge base underpins many AI systems, a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A knowledge base is a structured store of information that expert and AI systems reason from.

clue.text: Crown long cracked by salt

indicators.note: something cracked has a gap opened in it, which the next item fills

parts.note: to pine is to long for
NaCl is the chemical formula for common salt, sodium chloride

explanation.surface: A crown that has been split open by salt over time.
explanation.walkthrough: Salt here is the chemist's formula for sodium chloride, not seasoning.
explanation.definitionFit: Crown as in the top or summit of something; a pinnacle is the highest point.

clue.text: Punished lag — in new trial — one holding up bank

indicators.note: punished suggests being knocked about, so the letters are beaten into a new order

parts.note: the letters of these four words

explanation.surface: A convict given a retrial is punished for a bank robbery.
explanation.walkthrough: A lag is British slang for a convict; 'holding up bank' suggests an armed robbery but means supporting an earth bank.
explanation.definitionFit: A retaining wall is built to support a slope or bank of earth and stop it slipping.

clue.text: Unacceptable either way

indicators.note: something that works either way reads the same forwards and backwards

parts.note: the answer reads the same forwards and backwards, so the definition works read in either direction

explanation.surface: A flat refusal: this is unacceptable whichever way you look at it.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is a palindrome, so the clue is a definition plus a note that it reads the same from either end.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Not on' is a colloquial British idiom meaning not permissible or out of order.

clue.text: Diamond jubilee's finale follows very bright tune

parts.note: so means very, as in 'so good'
lit means illuminated, bright
an air is a melody

indicators.note: a finale is the closing part, so only the last letter of the word is kept

parts.note: the final letter of jubilee

explanation.surface: A sparkling song plays out the close of a Diamond Jubilee celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Follows' puts the jubilee's last letter after the rest; the Diamond Jubilee surface makes 'Diamond' look like part of a title rather than the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A solitaire is a single gem, typically a diamond, set on its own in a ring.

clue.text: Eccentric won't go for surprise

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or off-centre, so the letters that follow are put out of their usual order

parts.note: the letters of these words, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: Someone odd refuses to go along with a surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: To wrong-foot someone is to catch them off balance, taking them unawares.

clue.text: Stealthy spy girl Juliet enters

indicators.note: something that enters goes inside, so this letter is placed within the name

parts.note: a girl's name
Juliet is J in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A secret agent called Juliet slips quietly into a room.
explanation.walkthrough: J goes inside NINA, after its third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Ninjas were Japanese covert agents trained in espionage and stealth.

clue.text: Consistently, one appears thus among Moonies

definitions.meaning: first meaning: uniformly, at a steady rate
second meaning: the letters O, N, E sit at the even-numbered places (2nd, 4th, 6th) of Moonies

explanation.surface: A remark that a certain person always turns up among members of the Unification Church.
explanation.walkthrough: Moonies is a nickname for the Unification Church; here it is just a word whose even letters spell the number one.
explanation.definitionFit: Evenly as an adverb means in a uniform, steady way, which is what consistently describes.

clue.text: Oppressive demand from an exotic rogue

indicators.note: rogue means wayward or out of control, so these letters stray from their order

parts.note: the letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A foreign scoundrel makes an unreasonable claim on someone.
explanation.definitionFit: An exaction is the forceful extortion of money or goods, an excessive levy.

clue.text: Say Joy hugs Charlie ?

definitions.note: the printed clue shows the smiley :-) before the question mark, an example of the answer; the symbol is lost in this copy

indicators.note: to hug is to enclose in one's arms, so the first word wraps around the next letter

parts.note: joy is an example of a feeling, signalled by 'Say'
Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Joy embraces Charlie, followed by a smiley face.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue ends with a printed smiley :-) and a query: the definition is the symbol itself. C goes inside EMOTION after its fifth letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A smiley face typed with punctuation is the classic example of a text symbol conveying feeling.

clue.text: Noble brand connected to ship

parts.note: a marque is a make or brand, especially of car
SS is the prefix for steamship

explanation.surface: A posh label associated with a shipping line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Noble' looks like an adjective describing the brand but is a noun, the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A marquess is a British peer ranking above an earl and below a duke.

clue.text: Associate judge's first to block grand statute's weak feature

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for grand, a thousand

indicators.note: a blockage sits inside a passage, so these letters go inside the word for a statute

parts.note: a statute is a written law
ass. is a dictionary abbreviation for associate

indicators.note: first asks for only the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: the opening letter of judge

explanation.surface: A legal note about an associate judge stopping a grand statute because of a weakness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Associate judge' looks like a legal title, but the words split: an abbreviation for associate, then just the first letter of judge.
explanation.definitionFit: A boxer with a glass jaw is easily knocked out, so the phrase means a vulnerable point.

clue.text: Bar employee who's dodgy resents hysterical hosts

indicators.note: to host is to hold inside, so the words that come before contain the answer

parts.note: runs from the last letter of the first word into the second

explanation.surface: A shady barman resents a hysterical customer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' suggests a pub, but here it is the legal profession; the answer is a crooked lawyer.
explanation.definitionFit: A shyster is an unscrupulous lawyer, and the Bar is the body of barristers.

clue.text: Learnt about place for organ

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first word goes around the abbreviation

parts.note: seen in the sense of found out or discovered
Pl. is the street-name abbreviation for Place

explanation.surface: Someone has learnt where a particular organ is located in the body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Learnt' is used in the sense of discovered, as in 'I've seen that he left'.
explanation.definitionFit: The spleen is an abdominal organ that filters blood.

clue.text: Soft, mainly red sparkling wine that goes straight to one's heart?

definitions.text: that goes straight to one's heart?

indicators.note: mainly means most but not all, so the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: p for piano, soft in music
taken as written
Cava is a Spanish sparkling wine

explanation.surface: A gentle red fizz that goes straight to your head, or rather your heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goes straight to one's heart' reads as emotional, but it is anatomical. The precava is the superior vena cava, which carries blood straight to the heart.
explanation.definitionFit: The precava is the large vein returning blood from the upper body directly into the heart.

clue.text: University figure showing means of digital protection?

parts.note: the Massachusetts Institute of Technology
a number

explanation.surface: An academic from a technical university explains cybersecurity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Digital' suggests computing, but digits here are fingers.
explanation.definitionFit: A mitten keeps the fingers warm, protecting them as a glove would.

clue.text: Cottage near to old centre in northern parts

indicators.note: parts is a verb here: the letters split the preposition apart by sitting between its letters

parts.note: by means beside, near to
O is the abbreviation for old

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle, so only the central pair of letters is kept

parts.note: the two central letters of this eight-letter word

explanation.surface: A cottage near the old centre of a town somewhere in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parts' looks like a noun meaning regions but is a verb meaning splits. A bothy is a simple hut or cottage, especially in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: A bothy is a small, basic dwelling or shelter in Scotland, a kind of humble cottage.

clue.text: Many leave each week charged with case of fraudulence

indicators.note: something charged with a substance is loaded with it, so these letters are packed inside

parts.note: to quit is to leave
ea. is the abbreviation for each

indicators.note: a case is an outer shell, so only the outside letters of the word are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of fraudulence
W is the abbreviation for week

explanation.surface: Lots of staff walk out every week after being charged with fraud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charged with' reads as an accusation, but it means loaded: the edge letters of fraudulence are packed inside each-week.
explanation.definitionFit: Quite a few is an understated idiom meaning a fairly large number.

clue.text: Meeting because of … I can't recall

parts.note: for as in 'for that reason'
the hesitant noise of someone trying to remember

explanation.surface: Someone trying to remember why a meeting was called.
explanation.definitionFit: A forum is a gathering or assembly where ideas are discussed.

clue.text: See current in river is most erratic

parts.note: to spot is to see

indicators.note: in places the current's symbol inside the name of the river

parts.note: the Test is a river in Hampshire, southern England
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: An observation that the current in a river is at its most unpredictable.
explanation.walkthrough: The Test is a favourite crossword river; 'current' is the physicist's symbol, not the flow of water.
explanation.definitionFit: Spotty can mean patchy or uneven in quality, so the superlative means most inconsistent.

clue.text: Task for image developers in trouble for one month

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation inside the verb that follows

parts.note: to ail is to trouble or afflict
public relations is the job of people who manage someone's image

explanation.surface: Photographers in a darkroom struggle with a job for a whole month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Image developers' suggests photography, but it means publicists who shape a public image.
explanation.definitionFit: April is one of the twelve calendar months, so it is an example of the definition.

clue.text: Order gifts that branch plugs

indicators.note: a plug fills a gap, so the word for branch goes into the word for gifts

parts.note: presents are gifts
an arm is a branch, as of an organisation or river

explanation.surface: A request for presents that some department will supply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' is a noun: a military command, not a request for goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Present arms is a drill command telling soldiers to hold their rifles upright in salute.
